key_insight: Ba3HoRu2O9 shows a mixed excitation landscape where low-energy spin waves and higher-energy crystal-field, phonon, and molecular magnetic modes overlap, requiring multiple techniques to disentangle them.
engineering_relevance: The work provides a microscopic basis for tuning spin-dipole coupling and excitation spectra in 4d-4f multiferroic oxides, which is useful for designing functional quantum and magnetoelectric materials.
method: Inelastic neutron scattering tracked excitations across the meV range.
Linear spin-wave and Stevens crystal-field calculations assigned magnetic and Ho3+ transitions.
Raman spectroscopy and machine-learned force-field phonon calculations helped identify overlapping lattice modes.
evidence_signal: The low-energy dispersive mode below 6.2 meV matches linear spin-wave theory, while broad features near 20, 39, 70, and 90 meV persist above the magnetic ordering temperature.
watch_item: Because several excitation types overlap near 39 meV, any single-technique assignment would be ambiguous without combined neutron, Raman, and modeling analysis.
paper_title: Interplay of Spin Waves, Crystal-Field Excitations, and Phonons in Multiferroic Ba3HoRu2O9 revealed by Inelastic Neutron Scattering, Crystal-Field Analysis, and Machine-Learned Phonon Calculations
